classification.difficultyReason: Follow the supplied Pythagorean and explicit-differentiation scaffold, then substitute the 5–12–13 geometry and interpret or reverse the connected velocities.

content.prompt: A ladder 13 metres long rests against a wall, with its base $x$ metres from the wall and its top $y$ metres high.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why $x^2+y^2=169$, solve for $y$, and differentiate with respect to $t$.

answer.worked:
The wall and ground form a right angle, so Pythagoras gives
$$\begin{aligned}x^2+y^2&=13^2\\&=169,\\y&=\sqrt{169-x^2}.\end{aligned}$$
The positive square root is used because $y$ is a height. By the chain rule,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dt}&=\frac{dy}{dx}\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{169-x^2}}\frac{dx}{dt}.\end{aligned}$$

inlines.text: Hence find, when the base is 5 metres from the wall:

children.label: b
children.prompt: the rate at which the top is slipping down when the base is slipping out at 1 cm/s,

answer.worked:
When $x=5$,
$$\begin{aligned}y&=\sqrt{169-25}\\&=12\text{ m}.\end{aligned}$$
Using $\frac{dx}{dt}=1\text{ cm/s}$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dt}&=-\frac{x}{y}\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=-\frac{5}{12}(1)\\&=-\frac{5}{12}\text{ cm/s}.\end{aligned}$$
The top slips down at $\frac{5}{12}\text{ cm/s}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: the rate at which the base is slipping out when the top is slipping down at 5 mm/s.

answer.worked:
When $x=5$, $y=12$. Using $\frac{dy}{dt}=-5\text{ mm/s}$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dt}&=-\frac{x}{y}\frac{dx}{dt},\\-5&=-\frac{5}{12}\frac{dx}{dt},\\\frac{dx}{dt}&=12\text{ mm/s}.\end{aligned}$$
The base slips out at $12\text{ mm/s}$.
